How to Submit Public Comment

Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of
the following methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit
it to the City Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes
per person per item. At the Mayor’s discretion, the time limit may be shortened to allow
all speakers to address the City Council.

Website: Electronic submission of Public Comment is available via the City’s website
as noted below. Public Comment submitted electronically by 4:00 P.M. on the meeting
day will be forwarded to the City Council before the meeting for their consideration,
but will not be read during the meeting. Comments submitted after 4:00 P.M. will be
forwarded to Council but may not be received before the meeting.

Please submit your comments using the online public comment form at
Public Comment.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – March 18, 2025  1
   City Council Regular Meeting Agenda
  Tuesday, March 18, 2025

 •  CALL TO ORDER
 •  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE LED BY: Mayor Wu
 •  ROLL CALL: Mayor Wu, Vice Mayor Menchaca, Council Members Chan, Ding,
  Herrera Avila

 1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

 2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. RECOGNITION OF FIRE DEPARTMENT PROMOTION

 3. PUBLIC COMMENT

 4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  All items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and
  recommendations will be approved in one motion unless a member of the
  City Council requests separate discussion.

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the City Council
  meeting.

  1. Minutes of the Special City Council Meeting of March 4, 2025.
  2. Minutes of the Regular City Council Meeting of March 4, 2025.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action: Approval

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The most recent Material Demands from the Finance Department are presented
  to the City Council for review and approval.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – March 18, 2025  2
   Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Material Demands as
  presented.

  C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT – FEBRUARY 2025

  In accordance with the City of San Gabriel’s 2024-2025 Adopted Investment
  Policy (Resolution No. 24-35) and California Government Code Section 53646,
  the Finance Director is to render an investment report to the City Council, City
  Treasurer, City Manager, and the City Attorney. The Cash and Investment
  Report is presented to receive and file in accordance with the City’s adopted
  2025-25 Investment Policy.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the Cash and
  Investment Report for February 2025.

  D. APPROVAL OF FINAL PARCEL MAP NO. 82702, A SELF-STORAGE PROJECT
  LOCATED AT 414 SOUTH SAN GABRIEL BOULEVARD PLANNING CASE NO.
  TMAP19-008

  The development, located at 414 South San Gabriel Boulevard, is a 199,358-
  square-foot building with self-storage and an artist studio. City staff and the
  Los Angeles Department of Public Works have reviewed the Final Parcel Map
  and have determined it is in compliance with the State Subdivision Map Act,
  conditions of approval, and the City’s ordinances. There is no financial impact
  in processing a final map.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: The project has
  been reviewed for compliance with the California Environmental Quality Act
  (CEQA). The City has determined that the project would not have a significant
  effect on the environment due to mitigation measures incorporated through the
  adoption of the Final Mitigated Negative Declaration (MND) and Mitigation
  Monitoring and Reporting Program (MMRP).

  Recommended Action:

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – March 18, 2025  3
   Staff recommends that the City Council accept Final Parcel Map No. 82702 and
  authorize filing with the Los Angeles County Recorder.

  E. RESOLUTION NO. 25-11 PROCLAIMING THE TERMINATION OF A LOCAL
  EMERGENCY

  On January 7, 2025, and in the days following, the City of San Gabriel was
  impacted by a destructive wind and fire event. The Fire Chief activated the
  Emergency Operations Center (EOC) at Level 1 staffing on January 7, 2025, with
  Public Works, Police, Fire, and Administration duties coordinated from the EOC
  for the next two days. Due to continuing danger, on January 20, 2025, in
  cooperation with the County of Los Angeles Office of Emergency Management,
  the City Manager as Director of Emergency Services proclaimed the existence
  of a local emergency. The City Council ratified the proclamation on March 21,
  2025. Staff has determined that a state of local emergency no longer exists, and
  formal City Council action is requested to terminate the state of local
  emergency. There is no fiscal impact from the adoption of Resolution No. 25-
  11.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 25-11
  proclaiming the termination of a local emergency.

  F. 400-420 WEST VALLEY BOULEVARD REQUEST TO WAIVE DEVELOPMENT
  IMPACT FEE INCREASE IN THE AMOUNT OF $36,567.80

  The City Council is requested to consider a request from Chateau Operating
  Corporation to waive the development impact fee increase for a mixed-use
  development located at 400-420 West Valley Boulevard within the Valley
  Boulevard Specific Plan area in the amount of $36,567.80. If the City Council
  approves the request, the current balance of the Development Impact Fee
  account will decrease by $10,000.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: The proposed fee
  waiver request is categorically exempt from the California Environmental Quality
  Act (CEQA) pursuant to section 15061(b)(3) because it is covered by the
  commonsense exemption, where it can be seen with certainty that there is no
  possibility that the proposed amendment would have a significant effect on the
  environment, therefore it is not subject to CEQA.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – March 18, 2025  4
   Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council waive the development impact fee
  increase in the amount of $36,567.80 and authorize a refund of the $10,000
  paid into the Development Impact Fee account.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING – None.

 6. CONTINUED BUSINESS

  A. FENCES, WALLS, AND HEDGES HEIGHT DISCUSSION

  On January 21, 2025, the City Council considered Zone Text Amendment
  (ZTA24-004) relating to hedge heights in residential zones. The City Council
  continued the item and directed staff to gather additional information for
  further discussion at a future meeting. There is no fiscal impact as this is an
  information item only.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council provide comments or directions on
  fences, walls, and hedge heights in residential zones and within the public right-
  of-way or public sidewalk area.

 7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. FISCAL YEAR 2024-2025 MID-YEAR BUDGET UPDATE [RESOLUTION NO.
  25-13]

  The mid-year budget update report reviews the financial performance of the
  General Fund and the Mission Playhouse through January 31, 2025. The General
  Fund serves as the primary operating fund for the City. This update analyzes
  revenues and expenditure trends, incorporates additional appropriations since
  the budget’s adoption, and projects the financial results for the fiscal year
  ending June 30, 2025. The report also provides explanations for the changes
  reflected in the mid-year budget update.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – March 18, 2025  5
   Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends City Council receive and file the mid-year budget update
  report and adopt Resolution No. 25-13 approving mid-year adjustments to the
  fiscal year 2024-2025 budget.

  B. AUTHORIZATION OF TEMPORARY POLICE STAFFING INCREASE AND
  ADDITION OF HUMAN RESOURCE SPECIALIST POSITION TO THE
  DEPARTMENT’S AUTHORIZED PERSONNEL [RESOLUTION NO. 25-12]

  The Police Department is allotted 54 sworn officers. Due to projected vacancies
  within the coming months, the San Gabriel Police Department seeks approval
  to temporarily increase the number of sworn officers to 59. The temporary
  increase in staffing will allow for continuity as employees separate from the
  organization. In addition, the Police Department requests to increase its
  professional staffing level to include one Human Resources Specialist, who will
  be assigned to the Recruitment, Training, and Equipment Bureau, replacing the
  need for a sworn officer to staff this position. The estimated cost of a newly-
  hired sworn officer, including salary and benefits, is approximately $125,000.
  The total cost for five sworn officers would be $625,000. The cost for a Human
  Resources Specialist position ranges from $90,400 to $103,500, depending on
  the employee’s step placement.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends the City Council adopt Resolution No. 25-12 authorizing the
  City Manager and the Human Resources Director to temporarily over-hire 5
  police officers and to add a Human Resources Specialist to the Police
  Department’s staffing.

 8. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

 9. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
  general information and/or concern. This is also the time for Council Members to
  report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended.

 10. CLOSED SESSION – None.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – March 18, 2025  6
   11. ADJOURNMENT

  The next regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, April 1, 2025, at
  6:30 P.M. Information regarding matters to be considered at each meeting will be
  available on the Friday before the City Council Meeting on the City’s website at
  www.sangabrielcity.com.

MINUTES OF MARCH 18, 2025
  REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

I  CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Wu called the regular meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at 6:37 P.M.
  on Tuesday, March 18, 2025, in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 425 South Mission Drive,
  San Gabriel, California, 91776.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Mayor Wu .

  ROLL CALL

  Council Members Present:  Eric Chan, Tony Ding, Jorge Herrera Avila, Vice Mayor
  Menchaca, and Mayor John Wu.
  Council Members Absent:  None.
  Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto, City Attorney Keith
  Lemieux, Community Services Director Rebecca Perez,

I  Chief City Clerk Sharon Clark, Fire Chief Steven Wallace;
  Human Resources/Risk Management Director Edward
  Macias, Finance Director William Kaholokula, Police
  Chief Edward Elizalde, Acting Public Works Director/
  City Engineer Szeka Cheng, Acting Community
  Development Director Samantha Tewasart, and
  Assistant City Clerk Marilyn Bonus.

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT

  A. CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATOR (GOVERNMENT CODE §54957.6)

  City Negotiators - City Manager Lazzaretto, City Attorney Lemieux, and Human
  Resources/Risk Management Director Macias.

  Regarding the following Employee Organizations - San Gabriel Police Officer's
  Association, San Gabriel Police Management Group, San Gabriel Firefighter's
  Association, San Gabriel Fire Management Group and all Unrepresented Employees.

I  There was no reportable action.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS

  Chief City Clerk Clark provided information for the public on how to view the meeting.

  1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  Mayor Wu approved the agenda order.

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 1 of 5  March 18, 2025

  ____._.__,...._ _  .........
   2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. RECOGNITION OF FIRE DEPARTMENT PROMOTION

  Fire Chief Wallace made the presentation to Fire Engineer Kevin Montoya, and
  Chief City Clerk Clark administered a ceremonial oath of office. Fire Engineer
  Montoya's badge was pinned by his father, retired City of Orange Fire Captain
  Adrian Montoya.

I  3. PUBLIC COMMENT

  Chandler Weber, Public Information Officer, U.S. Small Business Administration, spoke
  on benefits the Administration can provide for business owners.

  Cheri Cabot, resident, on behalf of the Kiwanis Club of San Gabriel, as Chair of the
  Scholarship Committee, announced the Kiwanis scholarship program.

  4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  A motion was made by Vice Mayor Menchaca, seconded by Council Member Ding, to
  approve Consent Calendar Items 4A - 4F as presented.

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  CHAN, DING, HERRERA AVILA, MENCHACA, WU
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

I  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The City Council approved the following:

  1. Minutes of the Special City Council Meeting of February 18, 2025.
  2. Minutes of the Regular City Council Meeting of February 18, 2025.

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The City Council approved February 21, and 28, 2025, Material Demands for the
  payment of City expenditures.

  C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT - FEBRUARY 2025

  The City Council received and filed the Cash and Investment Report for February
  2025.

I  D. APPROVAL OF FINAL PARCEL MAP NO. 82702, A SELF-STORAGE PROJECT
  LOCATED AT 414 SOUTH SAN GABRIEL BOULEVARD PLANNING CASE NO.
  TMAP19-008

  The City Council accepted Final Parcel Map No. 82702 and authorized filing with
  the Los Angeles County Recorder.

  E. RESOLUTION NO. 25-11 PROCLAIMING THE TERMINATION OF A LOCAL
  EMERGENCY

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 2 of 5  March 18, 2025
   The City Council adopted Resolution No. 25-11 proclaiming the termination of a
  local emergency.

  F. 400-420 WEST VALLEY BOULEVARD REQUEST TO WAIVE DEVELOPMENT
  IMPACT FEE INCREASE IN THE AMOUNT OF $36,567.80

  The City Council waived the development impact fee increase in the amount of
  $36,567.80 and authorized a refund of the $10,000 paid into the Development
  Impact Fee account.

I  5. PUBLIC HEARING - None.

  6. CONTINUED BUSINESS

  A. FENCES, WALLS, AND HEDGES HEIGHT DISCUSSION

  Acting Community Development Director Tewasart made the presentation .

  Clarifying discussion included how removing height limits would affect public
  safety.

  Priscilla Geddis, resident, submitted written comments expressing various
  concerns.

  Discussion included hedge height as related to public safety, enforcement, and
  maintenance; the homeowner's right to landscape; public outreach about
  vegetation maintenance responsibility; hedge regulations in neighboring cities;
  and disputes on hedge height as civil matters.

I  There was a consensus of the City Council to direct staff to prepare an ordinance
  keeping fence and wall regulations unchanged and removing the height limit for
  hedges.

  7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. FISCAL VEAR 2024-2025 MID-VEAR BUDGET UPDATE [RESOLUTION NO. 25-
  13]

  Finance Director Kaholokula made the presentation.

  Clarifying discussion included changes in Transient Occupancy Tax (TOT) revenues.

  There was no public comment.

  Discussion included cost control measures; general fund reserve levels; projections
  are based on departments spending all appropriated funds; variability of plan
  check fees; property tax deferral of $125,000; and possible reimbursements from

I  FEMA related to the Eaton Fire.

  A motion was made by Council Member Chan, seconded by Vice Mayor Menchaca,
  to receive and file the mid-year budget update report and adopt Resolution No.
  25-13 approving mid-year adjustments to the fiscal year 2024-2025 budget.

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  CHAN, DING, HERRERA AVILA, MENCHACA, WU
  NOES:  NONE

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 3 of 5  March 18, 2025
   ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE
  B. AUTHORIZATION OF TEMPORARY POLICE STAFFING INCREASE AND
  ADDITION OF HUMAN RESOURCE SPECIALIST POSITION TO THE
  DEPARTMENT'S AUTHORIZED PERSONNEL [RESOLUTION NO. 25-12]

  Police Chief Elizalde made the presentation.

  Clarifying discussion included the Police Department's percentage of the City

I  budget, challenges of filling the roster of allotted sworn personnel, space
  limitations, overtime aspects, technology to improve efficiency, and vacancy
  savings.

  A written comment in opposition was received from Chasity Jennings-Nunez.

  Discussion included job details for the human resources specialist, staffing levels,
  hiring process for sworn positions, hiring challenges, similar over-hiring practices
  being used by other agencies, officer positions would be offset with vacancy
  savings and the human resources specialist position would be budgeted, and
  recruitment strategies.

  A motion was made by Vice Mayor Menchaca, seconded by Council Member Ding,
  to adopt Resolution No. 25-12 authorizing the City Manager and the Human
  Resources Director to temporarily over-hire five police officers and to add a Human
  Resources Specialist to the Police Department's staffing.

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

I  AYES:
  NOES:
  ABSTAIN:
  CHAN, DING, HERRERA AVILA, MENCHACA, WU
  NONE
  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  8. CITY MANAGER'S REPORT - None.

  9. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Council Member Chan reported on his attendance at a monthly Chinese American
  Citizens' Alliance meeting.

  Council Member Herrera Avila reported his attendance at the National League of Cities
  Conference and noted the topics that were presented and requested a discussion on
  Mayor Wu's proposed internship program be agendized for the next meeting.
  Following Vice Mayor Menchaca's request for more information outside of the agenda
  process, Council Member Herrera Avila withdrew his request. In closing, he thanked
  the Mayor for his year of service as Mayor.

I  Council Member Ding reported on his attendance at the 44 th Annual National Latina
  Women's Conference and Expo, and the grand opening of Seen Health San Gabriel
  Valley.

  Vice Mayor Menchaca reported on her attendance at the Mexican American
  Opportunity Foundation's National Latina Women's Conference and Expo held in San
  Gabriel, and the San Gabriel Mission High School's Career Day as the keynote speaker;
  and announced the San Gabriel Valley Mosquito and Vector Control Board's mosquito
  treatment campaign in the Eaton Fire burn area, and the San Gabriel Police Officers'

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 4 of 5  March 18, 2025
   Association's fundraiser and raffle event for San Gabriel Detective Greg Malette, to be
  held on March 19, 2024, from 11 :30 A.M. - 3:30 P.M. at the Mission Grape Vine Arbor.

  Mayor Wu reported on his attendance at the Chinese American Military Support
  Spring Festival and a Los Angeles County Sanitation District meeting; announced the
  Sanitation District's Earth Day Festival to be held on April 12, 2024, from 10:00 A.M. to
  2:00 P.M. at the District's main office in Whittier; and reported on his participatioij in
  the Asian American Real Estate Association Tri-County 2025 Gala and Installation
  Ceremony at the San Gabriel Country Club.

I  10. CLOSED SESSION - None.

  11. ADJOURNMENT

  The meeting was adjourned at 9:05 P.M.

  Respectfully submitted:

I

I

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 5 of 5  March 18, 2025
